style: A paid-ads testing lab where every frame is two variants: variant A in DM Serif Display on pale teal, variant B in heavy Sora on tomato, split by a line you can drag, with a method that forks into two lanes and merges into one winner. Light and dark.

concept.idea: Good paid ads are found, not guessed: two versions run side by side and the better one keeps the budget. The site is an A/B test of itself: the hero headline in two treatments, services as numbered tests, specialties as channels under test and a method that forks into A and B and merges into the winner.
concept.signature: The split hero: the same tagline set twice, as variant A and variant B, divided by a line with an A|B knob. It drifts slowly back and forth while nobody touches it, and the visitor can drag it (or use the arrow keys) to compare. Rests at the middle without JS or with reduced motion, still draggable.

jury.note: Self-score from the /jury rubric and shoot.mjs evidence (0 axe violations, no horizontal overflow at 390 or 1440 with sample and long.json, no tap target under 24 px, every focus stop visible, skip link first, nothing moving under reduced motion). No blind critic was run for this batch. The draggable A/B split is the idea itself, not decoration, and the method fork carries it through. The page below the hero is quieter and closer to a clean product page, so design is held at 7.5.
